Title: Verify that OTP generation for worker activation no longer returns the OTP in the API response
Section: Worker Management - OTP Generation and Verification
Preconditions: A worker with email 'worker@example.com' exists in the system but is not yet activated
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers/sendOtp with the payload in testData. Use a valid shopId where the authenticated user is the owner.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Test Worker",
  "phone": "+1234567890",
  "email": "worker@example.com",
  "address": "123 Test St",
  "role": "SHOP_WORKER"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 201 (Created) and a response body containing 'status: success', 'message: OTP sent to your email', and 'data: null'. The OTP is not exposed in the response.

Title: Verify that adding a worker with an existing email from the same shop returns an error and does not proceed
Preconditions: A worker with email 'worker@example.com' already exists and is assigned to the same shop (shopId) where the authenticated user is the owner
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the payload in testData. Use the same shopId as the existing worker's shop.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Test Worker",
  "phone": "+1234567890",
  "email": "worker@example.com",
  "address": "123 Test St",
  "role": "SHOP_WORKER"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Worker Already assigned to this shop'. No OTP is sent, and no new worker record is created.

Title: Verify that OTP verification for worker activation rejects mismatched PIN and Confirm PIN
Preconditions: A worker with phone number '+1234567890' exists, and a valid OTP has been generated and sent to the worker's email
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers/activate with the payload in testData. Use a valid shopId where the worker is expected to be activated.

Test Data: {
  "phoneNumber": "+1234567890",
  "pin": "1234",
  "confirmPin": "5678",
  "otp": "123456"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: PIN and Confirm PIN do not match'. The worker's PIN is not set.

Title: Verify that worker activation (PIN setting) enforces proper authorization - shop owner cannot activate a worker for a shop they do not own
Preconditions: A worker with phone number '+1234567890' exists in Shop B, and a valid OTP has been generated for the worker. The authenticated user is the owner of Shop A (not Shop B).
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers/activate with the payload in testData. Use shopId for Shop A (where the authenticated user is the owner).

Test Data: {
  "phoneNumber": "+1234567890",
  "pin": "1234",
  "confirmPin": "1234",
  "otp": "123456"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: You do not have permission to modify this shop'. The worker's PIN is not set.

Title: Verify that OTP verification for worker activation updates the worker's shop if a pending shop change request exists
Preconditions: A worker with email 'worker@example.com' exists in Shop B, and a pending shop change request to Shop A exists for this worker. A valid OTP has been generated for the worker's email. The authenticated user is the owner of Shop A.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers/activate with the payload in testData. Use shopId for Shop A.

Test Data: {
  "phoneNumber": "+1234567890",
  "pin": "1234",
  "confirmPin": "1234",
  "otp": "123456"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 201 (Created) and a response body containing 'status: success', 'message: Workers activated'. The worker's shop ID is updated to Shop A, and the pending shop change request is marked as completed.

Title: Verify that adding a worker with an existing email from another shop triggers a shop change request and sends a new OTP without exposing the OTP in the response
Preconditions: A worker with email 'worker@example.com' exists in Shop B. The authenticated user is the owner of Shop A.
Steps:
1. Send a POST request to /api/shops/{shopId}/workers with the payload in testData. Use shopId for Shop A.

Test Data: {
  "name": "Test Worker",
  "phone": "+1234567890",
  "email": "worker@example.com",
  "address": "123 Test St",
  "role": "SHOP_WORKER"
}
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 201 (Created) and a response body containing 'status: success', 'message: Workers added successfully', and 'data: null'. The worker receives an email with the OTP for shop change request, but the OTP is not exposed in the API response.
